raw_response:
I'm 45 this year, been farming since I was 20. Never went to school, can't read the fertilizer bags too well, but I know my 4.1 mu like the back of my hand. Me and my wife do most of the work. Our two kids—one's working construction in the county town, the other's still at home helping sometimes. Money's always tight, especially with fertilizer prices going up.

I split my land two ways. Got about 2 mu planted to cotton—that's where I make cash. The other 2.1 mu I did wheat last October, and after I cut that in June, I'll throw in maize right away. The wheat is mostly for our own flour, and the maize I sell some and keep some.

**Cotton:** I'll plant around April 20th when the soil warms up, same as always. I saved my own seed from last year—the big boll type that Old Wang down the road also grows. Saved me maybe 30 yuan per mu compared to buying new bags from the shop. I plow with my walking tractor and rake it smooth. At planting I put down about one and a half bags of compound fertilizer per mu. Last year I tried cutting back because cash was short, and my yield dropped bad—only got about 250 kg per mu while Liu got over 300. So this year I'm doing the usual amount, even if I have to borrow a little from my cousin. When flowering starts I'll topdress with another bag of urea. I irrigate twice, maybe three times if July is dry, but electricity for the pump is expensive so I watch it. For bugs I spray three or four times—aphids and bollworms always come. Picking is the hard part. Me and my wife can handle some, but for the main pick I'll hire two women from the village for about 6 days each. Costs me 80 yuan a day but otherwise the bolls sit too long.

**Wheat:** It's in the ground now, planted last October. I used my own saved seed—local wheat, not fancy hybrid. Costs almost nothing. Looking a bit yellow, so I'll water it once before jointing and throw down about half a bag of urea per mu as topdress. That's the way I always do it. Might spray once for disease if the spring stays wet. I expect around 400 kg per mu if the weather holds.

**Maize:** After I cut the wheat in early June, I got maybe a week to get the maize in. I'll rotary till quick and plant local seed—needs to mature fast before fall. I put compound fertilizer in the hole at planting, about one bag per mu. If July rains are good I might only irrigate once or twice. More than that and the electric bill eats my profit. One spray for weeds, that's usually enough. I hire the combine for wheat harvest but the maize I mostly manage myself.

This year I'm nervous about cash. The off-farm work from my kid helps, but fertilizer and hired picking labor are my big costs. I'd rather put a bit too much fertilizer than too little—losing a whole crop hurts way more than wasting a few yuan on extra urea. I'm not trying anything new. Same as last year, same as my neighbors, that's safe.
